title: AJAX Engineering Ltd - 544356 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Ajax Q2 FY27 revenue rose 9.5% to INR487 crores and PAT 30.4% to INR50.9 crores, while H1 EBITDA margin slipped to 11.5% amid steel-led cost inflation.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total revenue grew 9.5% YoY to INR487 crores, driven by volumes and price, with EBITDA up 13.7% to INR51.5 crores and PAT up 30.4% to INR50.9 crores. H1 FY27 revenue rose 5.5% to INR961.5 crores, but H1 EBITDA margin eased to 11.5% from 11.7% as raw material costs rose by close to mid-single digits. Management said state-level payment delays and capex slowdowns weighed on SLCM roads demand, while private-sector applications and non-SLCM products (pumps, batching plants) grew strongly. Price hikes of about 1% in September and 1% in November were taken on top of about 2% in Q4 FY26, with another 2% planned for Q4.

financial_highlights.metric: Spares and services revenue Q2 FY27

segments.name: SLCM
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue INR783.5 crores, +3.3% YoY, with 2.5% volume growth and benefit from the Q4 FY26 price hike. Retail market share rose to 75.5% in H1 FY27 from 70.7% in H1 FY26.

segments.name: Non-SLCM
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue INR103.5 crores, +31.5% YoY, led by concrete pumps; batching plants and boom pumps also contributed. Dealers sold pumps in 62 of 68 dealerships.

segments.name: Spares and services
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue INR74.6 crores, largely flat YoY; Q2 down 4.7% YoY to INR35.4 crores. Machine running hours fell about 25% YoY.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue grew 47% YoY in H1 FY27; export share of revenue was 7.4% in Q2 per management. Mix is 65% SLCM and 35% non-SLCM.

guidance_outlook: Management expects customer sentiment and demand to improve in H2; 60-65% of annual revenue typically comes in H2, so it asked to assess the business on an annualised and multi-year basis.
Management aspires to close FY27 with EBITDA margin close to double digits, but described H2 margin similar to H1 as a challenging task.
Steel prices rose from about INR58/kg to about INR70/kg; management anticipates a further rise to about INR75-76/kg, with a potential 2-3% commodity move.
Another price increase of about 2% is planned for Q4 FY27, with further pricing actions to be evaluated in a calibrated, phased manner.
Price hike benefits from September 2026 will start reflecting from Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: ARGO 4000 has been launched to fill a gap in the SLCM portfolio.
UDAAN series sales expanded to 20 states from 14, with H1 FY27 UDAAN volume at about 216 units versus about 49 units in H1 FY26.
A paver development is in progress with no firm launch timing; management aims to add at least one more paver unit in export markets this year.
Management did not disclose capacity, utilisation or capex plans on the call.
Cash of about INR1,150 crores is held for growth, including possible strategic inorganic opportunities.
demand_pricing: State government infrastructure spending is below budget and some states, notably Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, have large pending contractor payments. Volume growth came from Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh; softness was in Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar.

Application mix shifted away from roads: roads were about 70% of mix in FY25, 67% in FY26 and about 40% YTD FY27, while factories, buildings and urban infra rose to about 39% YTD FY27 from 13% in FY25 and 15% in FY26.
Top 10 states account for about 78% of SLCM volume. Uttar Pradesh plans small CC road contracts up to INR2,000 crores, and a circular pairs SLCMs with batching plants.
Price increases: about 2% in Q4 FY26, 1% in September 2026 and 1% in November 2026; management noted lags in passing through prices and dealer margin impact.
Raw material cost rose by close to mid-single digits in H1 FY27. Management said it expects steel to keep rising, which could pressure margins.
Spares and services were about 8-8.3% of revenue historically; FY24 about INR100-105 crores, FY25 about INR140 crores, FY26 about INR150 crores.
Financing: no challenges seen on wholesale or retail side; major retail financiers including HDFC, Kotak and Chola participate. Ajax has an A rating across its financier portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: Are there early signs of H2 demand recovery in October and November?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to growth in Gujarat, Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh, with Uttar Pradesh preparing about INR2,000 crores of small CC road contracts. Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh remain weak due to contractor payment delays. Management hopes to be close to double-digit EBITDA margin at year end.

qa_highlights.question: Can H2 margins match H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a challenging task because steel, aluminium, forex and geopolitics are uncertain, and steel is expected to rise further.

qa_highlights.question: Why did spares and services weaken and what will fix it?
qa_highlights.answer: Machine running hours fell about 25% YoY. Management is adding accountability across supply chain, parts availability and dealer units to restore the historical spares share of about 8-8.3% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is pricing enough to protect gross margin against inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about 3% cost inflation in H1 against price increases of 2% (Q4 FY26), 1% (September) and 1% (November), with another 2% planned for Q4. It noted that inflation could move in a 2-3% range and that pricing lags exist on deals already done.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export mix and growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are 65% SLCM and 35% non-SLCM. Kenya, Nigeria and Algeria make up about 40-42% of export volume; South Africa is targeted and LATAM ex-Brazil is under evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: How is UDAAN's TCO and application scope?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said UDAAN is mainly used in small rural roads, precast walls and brick manufacturing, and that labour savings pay back the machine in under three years. Solution selling with pumps for contractors is still being developed.

risks_watch: Steel prices rising toward INR75-76/kg could compress gross margin further if pricing lags.
Contractor payment delays in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, which management says must improve for H2 recovery.
Spares and services declining with machine running hours down about 25% YoY.
Uncertain H2 demand, with 60-65% of annual revenue in H2 and state capex below budget.
Dealer margin impact from price increases and the timing of the paver launch.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on the near term: management acknowledged state payment delays, margin pressure from steel and the difficulty of H2 margins, while staying confident on the medium term, market share gains and the non-SLCM and private-sector push. Answers on pricing and spares were specific, but questions on consulting, TCO and paver timing were answered in general terms.
key_quotes: We would definitely like to see ourselves in a strong position at the end of the year with close to about double digits.
It will be a challenging task, Vaibhav.
Our SLCM retail market share increased to 75.5% in H1 FY27, representing an expansion of approximately 480 basis points over the 70.7% in H1 FY26.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 EBITDA margin eased to 11.5% from 11.7% on ~3% cost inflation, management called H2 margin similar to H1 a 'challenging task', and steel is set to rise from INR70/kg to INR75-76/kg while the Q4 2% hike only partly offsets it.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No capacity, utilisation or capex plan was disclosed on the call; ARGO 4000 was launched as a product, and the paver has no firm launch timing.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 SLCM volumes grew 2.5% and non-SLCM revenue rose 31.5%, with UDAAN units up to ~216 from ~49, but roads were ~40% of application mix YTD FY27 and state payment delays persist in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management did not discuss capex plans; utilisation was not disclosed, though INR1,150 crores of cash is held for growth including possible inorganic deals.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management cut its FY27 end-state EBITDA aim to 'close to double digits' and gave no revenue number, with H1 revenue up only 5.5%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 margin was 11.5% against an aspiration of close to double digits by year end, and steel rising to INR75-76/kg could compress margins if price hikes lag (Sept hike only reflects from Q3 FY27).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: ARGO 4000 is already launched, and the paver is in development with a stated aim of one more export unit this year, but no firm launch date was given.

rows.label: Further ~2% price hike in Q4 FY27
rows.why: Management said another ~2% increase is planned for Q4 after ~2% in Q4 FY26, 1% in Sept and 1% in Nov 2026, against ~3% H1 cost inflation.

rows.label: Export growth and South Africa target
rows.why: Export revenue grew 47% YoY in H1 FY27 with 7.4% share in Q2, and South Africa is targeted while LATAM ex-Brazil is under evaluation.

rows.label: UP small CC road contracts up to INR2,000 crores
rows.why: Uttar Pradesh plans small CC road contracts up to INR2,000 crores and a circular pairs SLCMs with batching plants, but state payment delays in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh remain a drag.

tone.note: Management was confident on market share (SLCM retail share 75.5% vs 70.7%), UDAAN and non-SLCM growth and pricing actions, but cautious on H2 margins, steel costs and state payment delays; analysts pressed on H2 margin recovery and spares decline, and answers on paver timing and TCO were general.
